transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-08 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aditi Rao (Lead ML Eng, Nightingale), Markus Vogel (Platform Eng), Sienna Park (Product)

Auto Summary (brief) — may be partial: We walked through the Optimize console sandbox, ran two prebuilt scenarios (chat micro-concurrency + high-throughput API), discussed prefix cache (session KV) and lookahead prefetch, reviewed cost spreadsheet and showed where batching moves the unit econ. Security questions around KMS and VPC peering, next steps to run sims on Nightingale traces.

Topics / Agenda:
- Goals & constraints (Nightingale current stack, SLAs)
- Console demo: Optimize -> Prefetch playbook, Batch size slider, Cache TTLs
- Live sim: low-latency chat vs high-throughput inference
- Cost model walkthrough (per-token, reserved capacity, cache hit assumptions)
- Security/Q&A, next steps

Action items (readout): Listed separately.

Transcript body (timestamps rough, transcription has some imperfections):
[00:00] Sofia: hey everybody thanks for carving out time. quick intros from the redwood side — i'm sofia, i'll own the commercial side, and liam here is our solutions engineer who runs the econ sims — liam you wanna say hi?
[00:13] Liam: yeah hi all, liam chen, se. i'll jump into the console and run a couple of scenarios, demo the prefix or — we sometimes call it sessionization or prefix cash in the UI — apologies for the slip — and show impact on token cost and latency.
[00:28] Aditi: great thanks. just so you know our team is focused on a chat assistant and a high-throughput batch API. target 99p latency for chat < 200ms tail and throughput for API needs to be ~2k rps peak.
[00:40] Markus: also security — we require SOC2 plus KMS integration and we run in a VPC, so private deployment details will matter.
[00:52] Sofia: perfect, we'll keep those in mind. quick qual: what's your current model and infra?
[00:58] Aditi: we use a trimmed LLaMA-derived model in prod, quant to 8bit, hosted on k8s + gpu farm. we do some in-house caching but it's very ad-hoc.
[01:12] Liam: cool. the Optimize console has two levers we usually focus on — batching (which affects GPU utilization and per-token cost) and prefix/KV caching (which can avoid re-computation for repeated session prefixes). we'll show combined effects.
[01:28] Sienna: one question — are these recommendations safe for us to roll out without changing model weights? we can't re-train.
[01:35] Sofia: yes no model changes, everything is runtime and config — batch sizes, prefetch lookahead, cache TTL, routing policies.
[01:42] Liam: ok i'm sharing the optimize sandbox link now (note: link is demo-only) — https://console.redwood.ai/optimize/sandbox/ff-73b9
[01:55] Liam: starting scenario one: chat micro-concurrency. baseline: batch size 1, no prefix cache. metrics shown: p50 token latency 28ms, p95 230ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.85 (example numbers)
[02:12] Aditi: hm p95 230ms is above our target, that's interesting.
[02:16] Liam: right, so we bump batching to 4 (concurrency aware). you can see throughput increases and cost per token drops, but tail latency moves — however we can keep latency by using prefix cache for session histories.
[02:29] [02:29] (crosstalk) Markus: when you say prefix cache, is that the same as our internal session cache?
[02:33] Liam: similar idea — it's a KV cache keyed by session id + prefix hash. we store the KV pairs from the model's attention cache so incremental tokens skip large recompute. sometimes transcripts show as 'K V cache' etc, apologies.
[02:46] Aditi: any rough hit rate assumptions? our chats have a lot of repeated system prompts.
[02:52] Liam: hit rate depends — we ran with conservative 30% hit rate in the spreadsheet; in a lot of chat workloads with session reuse you'll see 50–70% often. i demoed a lookahead prefetch that warms the KV for predicted next-turns which boosted our effective hit to ~55% in this sandbox.
[03:10] Liam: switching to scenario two: high-throughput API with shorter prompts. baseline cost per 1k tokens $0.95 given small batch sizes, but ramping to batch size 16 with continuous batching and a little more latency budget drops unit cost by ~40%.
[03:27] Sienna: can you show the cost model inputs? like reserved GPU price vs on-demand?
[03:31] Liam: yep opening the cost tab — we have presets: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. for Dedicated we put a reserved GPU cost ($X/day) and amortize over tokens; for Hosted we use per-token list price. you can tweak concurrency distribution and cold-start factor.
[03:48] [03:48] Aditi: do you model prefix cache eviction? like TTLs and lookup costs? those look important for our long sessions.
[03:54] Liam: yes TTLs are a param. the model charges a small lookup egress and you can set TTL per tenant or route. in the sheet we model lookup cost as $0.00001 per lookup and TTL 30 minutes by default. eviction and compaction heuristics are also flagged.
[04:09] Sofia: quick note on security — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM. we also ingest audit logs into your SIEM via syslog or cloud watch.
[04:20] Markus: good. for VPC peering, any constraints on peering IP ranges?
[04:25] Liam: typical peering with a NAT gateway is fine; we'll provide ip ranges and a small config doc. we'll follow up with network runbook in the security packet.
[04:35] [04:35] Liam: now i want to run a live sim: i'm going to upload a small sample trace (this is anonymized pseudo-traffic) and run two sims: scenario A chat-heavy, scenario B api-heavy. running sim now — should take ~90s.
[04:52] (ambient typing sounds)
[05:15] Liam: sim done. results: chat-heavy: cache hit 48%, effective cost per 1k tokens $0.42, p95 latency 180ms. api-heavy: batch size 12 gave cost per 1k tokens $0.34, p95 320ms — there's a latency vs cost tradeoff.
[05:34] Aditi: the p95 320 on api-heavy is concerning but our API allows longer timeouts for batched jobs, so that could be acceptable.
[05:41] Sienna: are fallbacks available if the cache misses spike? we can't have customer-facing outages.
[05:45] Liam: yes — automatic fallback routing sends requests to a lower-latency model variant or to reserved capacity. policy driven. you can set SLO-based fallback thresholds.
[05:56] [05:56] Markus: curious about cold-starts — do you pre-warm kernels? we see big variance at start of hour.
[06:02] Liam: we support kernel pre-warm and keep-alive slots for burst capacity. Optimize recommends a small buffer (10–15%) of reserved instances during predicted peaks. we also show predicted warm-up latency in the sim chart.
[06:17] Aditi: what's the overhead of KV storage? if we store session KV for 1M users, that's a lot.
[06:24] Liam: right depends on average prefix size. in the cost sheet we estimate storage cost as $0.02 per active session per month for typical prefix sizes; this is configurable and you can compress KVs with quantization.
[06:38] Sofia: wanted to call out interplay with quantization — if you're on 8-bit kernels, caching may look a bit different — we provide quantization-friendly cache serialization.
[06:49] [06:49] Aditi: ok big picture — what are the recommended defaults for us?
[06:53] Liam: for chat-assistant: batch size 4, prefix TTL 20–30m, lookahead prefetch enabled for predicted next-turns, reserved buffer 15%. For API-heavy: batch size 12–16, session affinity off, use continuous batching with a 50ms batching window.
[07:10] Sienna: can we test the lookahead prefetch on our real traces?
[07:13] Liam: yes please share a 24h anonymized trace (as markus agreed) and we'll run two sims — we'll attach the exact sandbox config so you can reproduce locally or in your private deploy.
[07:24] (brief pause)
[07:32] Markus: security follow-up — will you share SOC2 reports and encryption-at-rest details?
[07:36] Sofia: yes we'll send the security pack; includes SOC2, ISO brief, KMS integration steps, and our network runbook.
[07:45] [07:45] (transcription artifacts: speaker labels sometimes swapped)
[07:52] Liam: now switching to the pricing slide — here's an example calc in the console: baseline on hosted @ $0.0012/token vs dedicated reserved at $0.0006/token after utilization. the spreadsheet models utilization gains from batching and hit rate from cache to show effective per-token spends.
[08:12] Aditi: can you share the spreadsheet formula? we'd like to plug our existing telemetry.
[08:16] Sofia: yes we'll share the Google Sheets link and a local CSV export.
[08:20] Liam: small gotcha — caching changes the semantics for some stateful tasks; we put a validation step in the console that flags prompts where caching might change output. it's conservative.
[08:33] Aditi: helpful — we have execs asking for clear % savings numbers. can you give a ballpark?
[08:38] Liam: on these traces: combined batching + prefix cache saved ~38–46% cost in chat scenario and ~30–40% in api-heavy depending on latency budget.
[08:53] Sienna: who on your team will help run the pilot?
[08:56] Sofia: liam and i will co-own pilot delivery; liam does the sims and engineering touchpoints; i'll handle access, pricing and commercial terms.
[09:05] [09:05] (minor cross talk) Markus: latency budgets — do you provide SLO dashboards?
[09:09] Liam: yes console has per-route SLO tracking, token-level cost breakdown, and traces. you can hook to Datadog or prometheus.
[09:18] Aditi: concerning compliance we might need to restrict cache TTLs to zero for certain tenants. can that be per-tenant?
[09:24] Liam: yes per-tenant and per-route TTLs, plus allowlisted routes for no-cache. policies can be pushed via the console API.
[09:34] Sofia: ok i'll recap next steps at the end, but quick question from me — timeline for pilot? what do you want?
[09:40] Aditi: short pilot: 2–3 weeks of sims and one live A/B with a small percent of traffic. we want cost estimates and a network checklist.
[09:48] Sofia: sounds good.
[09:50] [09:50] Liam: quick note — we sometimes mis-scan product names in transcrips, you'll see Redwood Optimize called Optima or Redwood Opti. ignore those.
[09:59] (laughter)
[10:02] Markus: any competitor concerns? we've talked to OtherAI, who pitched a single monolithic endpoint — but they don't have KV prefetching.
[10:10] Sofia: right benefit here is the unified runtime plus the Optimize toolkit that ties batch sizing, caching, and cost modeling together — you get pragmatic levers.
[10:20] Aditi: can we get an internal runbook for our infra team? network and KMS steps specifically.
[10:25] Sofia: yes that's in the security pack; we'll also add a one-page VPC peering checklist.
[10:31] [10:31] Liam: final demo note: i toggled lookahead prefetch off/on so you can see warm vs cold sessions in the chart. with lookahead on we reduced cold-start token work by ~22% in this trace.
[10:43] Sienna: impressive. from product POV this maps to better UX for multi-turn flows.
[10:48] Aditi: okay that's helpful. i'll coordinate the trace upload with markus.
[10:52] Markus: will do.
[10:55] Sofia: great — quick recap and next steps: 1) Sofia shares sandbox link, cost sheet, security pack (SOC2, KMS steps, VPC runbook) by Fri 10/10; 2) Nightingale to upload anonymized 24h trace by Thu 10/9; 3) Liam will run sims and share detailed logs and recommended config by 10/15; 4) schedule security review call week of 10/13.
[11:18] (wrap-up)
[11:25] Aditi: thanks all, this was productive.
[11:27] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and calendars.
[11:31] End of recording.

References shared during call:
